study_identification_part.si_4_title: Linking Personalized Brain Atrophy to Schizophrenia Network and Treatment Response

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: A vertex-wise general linear model (GLM) of cortical thickness was established for healthy subjects using age and gender as covariates. The normative model parameters (beta term maps for age and gender, and residuals) were used to calculate a vertex-wise W-score for each patient, where W-score = (expected - actual) / RSD.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: we first established a vertex-wise general linear model (GLM) of CT for the healthy subjects using age and gender as covariates (figure 1A). Next, parameters of the normative model (ie, beta term maps for age and gender, and residuals) were used to calculate a vertex-wise W-score for the CT of each patient (a W-score is a z-score adjusted for age and gender) using the formula: W-score = (expected-actual)/RSD
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Ji2023.pdf.md: Materials and methods / Atrophy Map and Network

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Cortical thickness (CT) was computed by measuring the distance between the white matter and pial surfaces at approximately 160,000 vertices using FreeSurfer 6.0. The cortical thickness was chosen as the response variable because it has been shown as a sensitive index for identifying individualized abnormality in schizophrenia.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: CT was computed by measuring the distance between the white matter and pial surfaces at approximately 160 000 vertices. ... The CT rather than other structural measures were used here since it has been shown as a sensitive index for identifying individualized abnormality in schizophrenia.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Ji2023.pdf.md: Materials and methods / MRI Data and Preprocessing; Atrophy Map and Network

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative model used age and gender (sex) as the only covariates in a linear model. The W-score formula explicitly shows: expected = age × β_age + gender × β_gender.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: we first established a vertex-wise general linear model (GLM) of CT for the healthy subjects using age and gender as covariates ... expected is the predicted CT with the application of the nuisance factors and beta weights from the regression in healthy controls (ie, age× β age + gender× β gender )
